target_audience: Undergraduate students in Mathematics or Education majors

sections.title: Introduction: The 'Bridge' Metaphor (0:00-0:45)
lecture_lines: Mathematical explanation bridges abstract symbols to intuition.
animations: Create a glowing bridge object in the center #FFFFFF.
Animate a signal moving across the bridge #FFFF00.
Place two distinct nodes at bridge ends #00FFFF.

sections.title: Criterion 1: Precision and Logical Mapping (0:45-2:00)
lecture_lines: Map every symbol to a concept.
Variables are dynamic entities, not just placeholders.
animations: Fade in a logical mapping diagram #00FF00.

sections.title: Criterion 2: The Power of Multiple Representations (2:00-3:30)
lecture_lines: Use the Rule of Three strategy.
Represent concepts algebraically, geometrically, and contextually.
animations: Show three different shapes for one concept #FF9900.
Rotate the shapes to show different perspectives #99FF00.
Consolidate the shapes into one core unit #0099FF.

sections.title: Criterion 3: Reducing Cognitive Load via Scaffolding (3:30-4:30)
lecture_lines: Break complex proofs into digestible chunks.
animations: Highlight a complex task being simplified #FF5555.
Animate the reduction of cognitive steps #55FF55.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Feedback Loop (4:30-5:00)
lecture_lines: Effective teaching is an iterative process.
Observe audience response to adjust complexity.
animations: Pulse the arrow to signify continuous growth #55FFFF.
Highlight the final completed goal icon #FF55FF.
